record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the Dirichlet problem −Δu + 1/u^α = λ f(x) in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, in the regime 0 < α < 1 where maximal positive solutions are known to exist for sufficiently large λ, do there also exist additional solutions beyond the maximal positive branch, either other positive solutions or free-boundary/compact-support solutions?

evidence.quote: It is easy to show that there are no solutions for λ > 0 small enough, but it remains the problem of the possible existence of more solutions, either positive or with compact support.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 1$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, let $f \in L^\infty(\Omega)$ with $f \ge 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, let $\lambda > 0$ be a real parameter, and fix an exponent $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Consider the singular semilinear Dirichlet problem
$$-\Delta u + \frac{1}{u^\alpha} = \lambda\, f(x) \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u \ge 0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega,$$
where the singular term $1/u^\alpha$ is interpreted as $0$ on the set $\{u = 0\}$ (so that nonnegative solutions with compact support / free boundary inside $\Omega$ are admissible). It is known that for $\lambda$ sufficiently large there exists a maximal positive solution $u_\lambda$ of this problem, while for $\lambda > 0$ small enough there are no solutions.

Question: For $\lambda$ in the existence regime (large enough), do there exist solutions other than the maximal positive solution? More precisely, determine whether there must exist either (i) an additional strictly positive solution different from the maximal one, or (ii) a nonnegative solution with compact support in $\Omega$ (a free-boundary solution), and if so, describe the structure of such additional branches as a function of $\lambda$.
artifact.status_search_result: The multiplicity question for the singular absorption Dirichlet problem with $0<\alpha<1$—whether additional positive solutions or free-boundary (compact-support) solutions exist beyond the known maximal positive branch—is posed as an open problem in the overview of this topic, and recent literature on related singular quasilinear problems addresses partial results (existence of branches of positive and free-boundary solutions) without resolving the multiplicity question in this regime. No source found establishing a complete answer.

status_evidence.title: Positive and Free Boundary Solutions to Singular Nonlinear Elliptic Problems with Absorption: An Overview and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Overview and open problems on singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption.
status_evidence.claim: The multiplicity question for 0<α<1 is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Branches of positive and free boundary solutions for some singular quasilinear elliptic problems
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and multiplicity of strictly positive or free-boundary solutions of some singular problems.
status_evidence.claim: Related quasilinear singular problems have partial multiplicity/free-boundary results, but not for this exact semilinear case in the stated regime.
